title: Floodgate throttles and adaptive reservation plan to prevent GPU pool floods
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a hosted API capacity incident on 2025-02-08 we observed rapid GPU pool saturation driven by an emergent tenant pattern: a short-lived burst of large-prefetch embedding requests combined with KV-cache pollution from long-context chat runs. The result was an 8-minute period where tail latency spiked, a ~30% increase in GPU queue depth, and cascading throttles that affected multi-tenant fairness for other workloads. This ticket captures proposed mitigations, tested implementations, rollouts, and postmortem action items.
comments: 2025-02-09 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage shows correlated spikes in prewarm/prefetch traffic and cache eviction rates in pool eu-west-1-gpu-A. We identified Tenant-451 as top contributor. Logged metrics and captured traces: gpu_queue_depth, admission_rejects, kv_cache_eviction_rate.

2025-02-10 - Marco Ruiz: Temporary mitigation: applied soft cap of 6 concurrent prefetch slots per tenant and increased admission fast-fail threshold from 120s to 90s. Immediate reduction in queue amplification observed but tail latency still above SLO for 2 tenants.

2025-02-12 - Grace Lin (SRE): Ran staged replay of tenant burst using synthetic harness; reproduced queue buildup at 80% of production rate. Confirmed that current autoscaler hysteresis causes delayed scale-up during short bursts.

2025-02-18 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype 'floodgate' admission controller implemented in admission-service branch (PR #988). Floodgate enforces short-window adaptive throttles based on moving-window GPU occupancy and per-tenant prefetch credit burn-rate.
2025-02-25 - DS team (Data Science): Provided traffic profiles and recommended moving-average window sizes (30s) and credit decay half-life (45s) for better responsiveness to bursts.

2025-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Canary rollout plan approved. Metrics to watch: per-pool queue depth, tenant rejection rate, 99th percentile latency, eviction rate of KV cache, and error budget burn. Canary in staging for 48h then eu-west-1 small pool for 24h before global rollout.

2025-03-08 - Marco Ruiz: Post-canary observations: floodgate reduced peak queue depth by 22% and cut eviction spike amplitude. Side effect: small increase in client fast-fails for interactive chat tenants; adding informative error payloads and SDK retry guidance.
2025-03-12 - Product (Nina Gomez): Need to coordinate customer comms and update status page messaging for tenants likely affected by new prefetch limits. Draft prepared.
2025-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Merged PRs related to metrics and dashboards: #1012 (floodgate telemetry), #1020 (per-tenant credit dashboard). Next: autoscaler hysteresis tuning PR #1031 awaiting review.

2025-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Blocking: validate scaling stability under mixed workloads and confirm no regressive latency for low-volume customers. Running longer-duration soak in staging cluster for 72h.
decisions: Adopt 'floodgate' short-window adaptive admission controller as primary first-line defense against burst-driven GPU pool floods.
Introduce a per-tenant soft reservation system to preserve minimum steady-state throughput for long-lived interactive tenants during bursts.
Tune autoscaler hysteresis to favor faster ramp-up for short bursts (reduce cool-down from 5m to 90s) while keeping scale-down conservative to avoid oscillation.
Expose informative fast-fail error codes and SDK guidance so clients can apply exponential backoff or ask for degraded modes instead of blind retries.
next_steps: Finalize autoscaler hysteresis tuning and land PR #1031 (Marco) - due 2025-03-15.
Complete rollout of floodgate to all hosted pools with progressive ramp and monitoring alerts (Aisha/Marco) - target 2025-03-20.
Add per-tenant prefetch visibility to Console (Frontend ticket) and create default prefetch guardrails (PM/Nina) - deliverable 2025-04-01.
Run cross-tenant fault-injection tests and long soak for 72h in staging to validate no regression for low-volume customers (SRE) - start 2025-03-13.
Prepare customer communications for tenants that will see stricter prefetch limits and provide guidance for batching and retry strategies (Customer Success/Nina) - draft 2025-03-17.
retrospective_summary: Root cause: a short-duration tenant burst that combined aggressive prefetching and long-context chat runs caused KV cache churn and a spike in per-request GPU occupancy. Contributing factors: autoscaler hysteresis tuned for long bursts causing delayed capacity priming, lack of short-window admission controls, and insufficient prefetch visibility in Console. Actions taken: implemented floodgate admission controller, added per-tenant soft reservations, tuned autoscaler hysteresis, improved telemetry and dashboards, and prepared customer-facing guidance. Expected impact: reduce incident frequency and tail latency for cross-tenant bursts while providing clearer failure modes for clients.
acceptance_criteria: Staged rollout shows >=20% reduction in peak pool queue depth during synthetic bursts.
No regression in 95th/99th latency for low-volume interactive tenants after 72h soak.
Per-tenant credit dashboard available in Console and exposes top 10 prefetch consumers.
Customer guidance published and CS playbook updated with remediation steps for tenants hitting prefetch caps.
